facts.claim: The WMO World Weather Information Service publishes climatological normals for Punta Cana (Dominican Republic) itself, supplied by the Oficina Nacional de Meteorología (ONAMET), the Dominican national meteorological service.

WMO WWIS remarks for Punta Cana: climatological information is based on monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990, and 'mean number of rain days' means the mean number of days with at least 1 mm of rain. WWIS cautions that averaging periods and rain-day definitions may differ between countries, so care is needed when comparing city climatologies.
Punta Cana, January (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 21.9 C, mean daily maximum 27.7 C, mean total rainfall 66.4 mm, mean 10.0 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, February (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 21.8 C, mean daily maximum 27.6 C, mean total rainfall 54.2 mm, mean 6.8 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, March (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 22.0 C, mean daily maximum 28.1 C, mean total rainfall 54.2 mm, mean 6.7 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, April (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 22.5 C, mean daily maximum 28.7 C, mean total rainfall 69.2 mm, mean 6.6 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, May (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 23.2 C, mean daily maximum 29.6 C, mean total rainfall 124.4 mm, mean 10.1 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, June (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 24.1 C, mean daily maximum 30.3 C, mean total rainfall 103.9 mm, mean 9.2 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, July (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 24.6 C, mean daily maximum 30.5 C, mean total rainfall 78.3 mm, mean 9.1 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, August (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 24.8 C, mean daily maximum 30.7 C, mean total rainfall 103.1 mm, mean 10.0 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, September (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 24.4 C, mean daily maximum 30.9 C, mean total rainfall 101.7 mm, mean 10.4 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, October (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 23.6 C, mean daily maximum 30.5 C, mean total rainfall 152.1 mm, mean 11.4 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, November (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 23.2 C, mean daily maximum 29.4 C, mean total rainfall 116.6 mm, mean 11.5 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Punta Cana, December (WMO WWIS, ONAMET, 1961-1990 normals): mean daily minimum 22.3 C, mean daily maximum 28.1 C, mean total rainfall 78.5 mm, mean 11.0 rain days (days with at least 1 mm).
Per the WMO WWIS Punta Cana table (1961-1990), mean daily maximum temperatures are lowest in February (27.6 C) and January (27.7 C) and highest in September (30.9 C) and August (30.7 C).

Per the WMO WWIS Punta Cana table (1961-1990), the wettest month by mean rainfall is October (152.1 mm, 11.4 rain days) followed by May (124.4 mm); the driest are February and March (54.2 mm each, 6.8 and 6.7 rain days).
US National Hurricane Center: 'The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30.' The Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea and Gulf of America.

US National Hurricane Center: tropical cyclone activity sometimes occurs before and after the official June 1 to November 30 season; the peak of the Atlantic hurricane season is September 10, with most activity occurring between mid-August and mid-October.

US National Hurricane Center: based on the 1991-2020 climate period, an average Atlantic season has 14 named storms, 7 hurricanes and 3 major hurricanes; formation dates in individual seasons can vary considerably from the averages.

Smartraveller (Australian Government), checked 24 November 2026 (page shows 'Updated: 25 February 2026'): overall advice level for the Dominican Republic is 'Exercise a high degree of caution' due to the threat of violent crime.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: 'You must buy a tourist card on arrival. It's valid for 30 days. Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. You should contact the nearest high commission/embassy or consulate of the Dominican Republic for the latest details.'

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: 'To enter and exit the Dominican Republic, you must complete the electronic entry and exit form, which shares information on your health and stay with local authorities' (form at eticket.migracion.gob.do).

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: exit requirements apply to children aged under 18 travelling alone, with one parent or with another adult; ask the nearest Dominican Republic embassy or consulate about the regulations before travel.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: 'The hurricane and rainy season is from June to November' and 'Tropical storms and hurricanes can happen in other months'; it also states 'The wet season is from May to November.' If there is a hurricane or severe storm, travellers may get stuck, flights could be delayed or cancelled, and flights out may fill quickly.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: the Dominican Republic experiences earthquakes, and tsunamis may occur; near the coast, move immediately to high ground if advised or on natural warning signs, without waiting for official alerts.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: mosquito-borne illnesses, including dengue and malaria, are common during the wet season from May to November; Zika virus is widespread and pregnant travellers should discuss plans with their doctor.
Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: many beaches have strong and dangerous rips, and lifeguards aren't present at some hotels, resorts and public beaches.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: when travelling to the airport use official airport taxis or ride share services and travel during daylight hours; use ride share, pre-booked taxis or hotel-provided transport, not unofficial taxis or 'carros publicos'.
Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: Australian dollars can't be exchanged for Dominican pesos (DOP); exchange US dollars at banks or official exchange offices and take US dollars with you.

Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: the Embassy of Canada in Santo Domingo provides consular assistance for Australians and can issue provisional travel documents; consular assistance is also available from the Australian Embassy in Mexico.
Smartraveller, checked 24 November 2026: get comprehensive travel insurance that covers all medical costs overseas, including evacuation; the Australian Government will not pay these costs.

insider_details.detail: For the driest, mildest wedding weather, the official Punta Cana normals point to February and March: about 54 mm of rain and fewer than 7 rain days a month, with average highs around 27.6 to 28.1 C. Plan outdoor ceremonies in this window if the guest list allows.

October is the wettest month in the official record (152.1 mm over about 11 rain days) and sits inside the NHC's mid-August to mid-October peak of hurricane activity. A September or October date needs a confirmed indoor or covered rain plan and flexible guest travel insurance.

Even in the hottest months (August and September) mean daily highs sit around 30.7 to 30.9 C, so the issue is humidity and sun rather than extreme heat. Schedule outdoor ceremonies for late afternoon and build shade and water stations into the run sheet (planning advice, not a sourced fact).

Every guest must complete the Dominican Republic's electronic entry and exit form and buy a tourist card on arrival (valid 30 days, per Smartraveller as at November 2026). Put both in the guest travel pack early; the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements before you book.
Book group airport transfers with official or pre-arranged operators and land guests in daylight where possible, as Smartraveller advises daylight airport travel and warns against unofficial taxis.
Tell guests to bring US dollars rather than Australian dollars for tips and incidentals, since Smartraveller says AUD can't be exchanged for Dominican pesos.
